name: Lemon Squeezy
tagline: Sell a digital product with Stripe while explicitly leaving tax remittance to the creator

pricing.notes: No fixed monthly subscription; fees are transaction based.

tiers.name: Ecommerce
tiers.limits: No published product or revenue cap; 5% + $0.50 per transaction as merchant of record.

tiers.name: Email 0-500 subscribers
tiers.limits: Up to 500 subscribers and 5,000 email sends per calendar month.

tiers.name: Email 501+ subscribers
tiers.limits: Pricing scales with total subscriber count above 500; numeric brackets did not render in the live calculator.
tiers.notes: Monthly and annual billing are offered.

tiers.name: Custom / Volume
tiers.limits: Custom high-volume commerce terms; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Ecommerce has no monthly fee or published usage cap; Email is free up to 500 subscribers and 5,000 sends per calendar month
pricing.billingTerms: ecommerce is transaction-only; Email offers monthly + annual billing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Base commerce fee is 5% + $0.50, with +1.5% for international payments, +1.5% for PayPal and +0.5% for subscriptions; non-US Stripe payouts add 1%, PayPal payouts add $0.50 in the US or 3% capped at $30 elsewhere; recovered carts add 5%, merchant affiliate referrals add 3%, and affiliate payouts add 2%; Email send limits are 10× the plan's subscriber allowance, and exceeding the subscriber cap triggers an automatic plan upgrade.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Lemon Squeezy, sell a digital product with Stripe while explicitly leaving tax remittance to the creator. The hard boundary is merchant-of-record tax, payments, fraud, licensing, subscriptions, and global compliance, plus payments, tax, distribution, and operations.
coreLoopDIY: Sell a small catalog of digital products through Stripe, deliver purchased files or lessons, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront, leaving tax remittance explicitly to the creator.
whatYouLose: merchant-of-record tax, payments, fraud, licensing, subscriptions, and global compliance
ongoingBurden: checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Lemon Squeezy because creators pay to outsource the dangerous and tedious parts around money, delivery, tax, and customer access. The recurring cost buys checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Active open-source commerce platform with modular checkout and fulfillment primitives.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Download sales and payment pages without a platform cut; email, storage and tax administration remain on your list.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit does not remit sales tax or provide merchant-of-record operations, and production media/email require separate services.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Easy Digital Downloads
alternatives.desc: A free WordPress download shop using ordinary payment gateways; tax remittance remains your character-building exercise.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Digital products, hosted checkout and delivery on a permanent free plan; taxes stay emphatically yours.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: systeme.io does not assume merchant-of-record duties or tax remittance, and its checkout is less developer/product focused.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: Digital products, licence files and checkout in one self-hosted shop; it will not remit taxes or run itself.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb does not provide merchant-of-record tax handling, fraud operations or managed checkout; the seller remains the merchant.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

alternatives.name: WooCommerce
alternatives.desc: A user-owned digital storefront with no merchant-of-record magic and no platform rent.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FOSSBilling
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Downloads, licences and billing fit, but the maintainers still call it beta and warn about rough edges.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A developer commerce platform, not a finished digital-product checkout and delivery product.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Polar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The hosted version charges 5% plus 50 cents per sale; the free self-hosted route is built for developers.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Merchant of record plan and a single-creator storefront DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Lemon Squeezy in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Stripe Checkout, and S3-compatible storage; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sell a small catalog of digital products through Stripe, deliver purchased files or lessons, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront, leaving tax remittance explicitly to the creator.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement products, variants, prices, files or lessons, coupons, customers, orders, and entitlements.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout and verify every webhook signature and idempotency key.
Grant access only after confirmed payment and revoke it on refund or chargeback.
Create a customer library with signed short-lived download or lesson URLs.
Add order search, resend receipt, refund handoff, export, and an immutable event log.
Document taxes as the creator's responsibility and do not calculate unsupported jurisdictions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out merchant-of-record tax remittance.
Deliberately leave out a buyer marketplace or affiliate network.
Deliberately leave out advanced communities, certificates, mobile apps, and enterprise learning features.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
